title: PRAC recommendations on signals adopted at the 13-16 May 2019 PRAC meeting
authors: European Medicines Agency, Pharmacovigilance Risk Assessment Committee
funder: not stated; a recommendation of the EU medicines regulator's pharmacovigilance committee
result: Signal 1.3 (EPITT 19277), adopted 16 May 2019: having considered EudraVigilance, literature, social media and cumulative reviews from marketing authorisation holders, PRAC required holders of products containing citalopram, escitalopram, fluvoxamine, fluoxetine, paroxetine and sertraline, and the SNRIs duloxetine, venlafaxine, desvenlafaxine and milnacipran, to add to SmPC section 4.4: 'SSRIs/SNRIs may cause symptoms of sexual dysfunction. There have been reports of long-lasting sexual dysfunction where the symptoms have continued despite discontinuation of SSRIs/SNRI', and to the package leaflet that in some cases these symptoms have continued after stopping treatment. Signal 1.4 (EPITT 19341): maculopathy added to the sertraline SmPC section 4.8 with frequency not known, and partial loss of vision to the leaflet.
